prerequisites: A basic understanding of programming, particularly familiarity with variables, data types, control structures, and functions.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the main constructs of Java and the principles of object-oriented programming.
Read and understand Java code, model a problem, and design, develop, and test a software solution.
Compare alternative solutions, select appropriate methods and tools, and justify their design decisions.
Critically evaluate code and suggestions produced by AI assistants and verify that they are correct and appropriate for the problem.
Describe how software works and explain their design decisions using appropriate technical terminology.
Consult technical documentation, deepen their understanding of course topics, and independently explore new software development tools.

syllabus_topics: Java fundamentals: data types, operators, control structures, methods, arrays, strings, and unit testing with JUnit
Object-oriented programming: classes, encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, interfaces, abstract classes, and composition
Java Collections Framework, generics, exception handling, and resource management
Functional and concurrent programming: lambda expressions, the Stream API, threads, synchronization, and concurrent task management
Graphical user interface development with JavaFX
Developing REST services with Spring Boot
Integrating REST services with JavaFX clients
assessment_rules: Assessment consists of a paper-based written exam and an individual take-home project. The written exam consists of ten multiple-choice or short-answer questions, each worth 3 points, for a total of 30 points. The project can raise or lower the written exam score by up to 3 points, depending on whether it is assessed as above or below average. Students are required to use AI assistants to complete the project.
